# Task

## Issue: legacy accounts can't be found by email, backfill needed

Users migrated from the legacy system can't log in: `lookup.find_by_email(conn, "Ann@Example.com")` returns nothing because `normalize_email` doesn't lowercase. Fix `normalize_email`, then run `scripts/migrate_accounts.py` to backfill the `accounts` table from `legacy_accounts` so the lookups work against the real data.

Follow the README and CONTRIBUTING, and confirm with the tests. There is no internet access.

When you're done, finish with a short pull-request description for the reviewer: what you changed, how you tested it, and any side effects a reviewer should know about.

from acctsvc import db
from acctsvc.lookup import find_by_email
from acctsvc.normalize import normalize_email

conn = db.connect('data/accounts.db')
print('normalize test', normalize_email('Ann@Example.com'))

# test lookup for a known migrated user
# User.1 should be normalized to user.1@example.com
for email in ['User.1@Example.COM', 'user.1@example.com', 'USER.1@EXAMPLE.COM', ' Ann@Example.com ', 'user.3@example.com']:
    res = find_by_email(conn, email)
    print(email, '->', res)

# also check counts
print('legacy', conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM legacy_accounts').fetchone())
print('accounts', conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts').fetchone())
# check that emails are lowercased
print(conn.execute('SELECT email FROM accounts LIMIT 5').fetchall())
# check plan normalization
print(conn.execute('SELECT DISTINCT plan FROM accounts').fetchall())
# check name normalization
print(conn.execute('SELECT name FROM accounts WHERE id=1').fetchone())

# Check the bad ids are skipped
for bad_id in [311, 702, 1049]:
    print('bad id', bad_id, conn.execute('SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id=?', (bad_id,)).fetchone())

conn.close()
